\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना} (giraftār karnā)}{गिरफ़्तार करना (giraftār karnā)}]{\hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना} (giraftār karnā) — to arrest}

\label{lesson:HI-C295-giraftarkarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for evidence, then the Hindi for to search for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना}}
\textbf{\hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना}} — \emph{giraftār karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{पुलिस} \hi{उसे} \hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करेगी} \hi{तो} \hi{वह} \hi{जेल} \hi{जाएगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar pulis use giraftār karegī to vah jel jāegā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the police arrest him, he will go to prison.
\end{quote}

Past, with \hi{ने} (he or she …): \hi{उसने} \hi{चोर} \hi{को} \hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{किया}, \emph{usne cor ko giraftār kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना}} (\emph{giraftār karnā}) is Persian \emph{giriftār}, \textquotedblleft{}seized, taken captive\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to the Persian verb for taking hold, with \textbf{\hi{करना}}. The person arrested takes \textbf{\hi{को}}: \textbf{\hi{चोर} \hi{को} \hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{किया}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{giraftār karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{giraftār karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar pulis use giraftār karegī to vah jel jāegā.} — If the police arrest him, he will go to prison.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for evidence, then the Hindi for to search for, then say \emph{giraftār karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To arrest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{मुक़दमा} (muqadmā)}{मुक़दमा (muqadmā)}]{\hi{मुक़दमा} (muqadmā) — a court case; a lawsuit}

\label{lesson:HI-C295-muqadma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to search for, then the Hindi for to arrest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{मुक़दमा}}
\textbf{\hi{मुक़दमा}} — \emph{muqadmā} — \textquotedblleft{}a court case; a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अदालत} \hi{में} \hi{चोर} \hi{का} \hi{मुक़दमा} \hi{दो} \hi{साल} \hi{से} \hi{चल} \hi{रहा} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{adālat meṁ cor kā muqadmā do sāl se cal rahā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief's case has been going on in court for two years.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{मुक़दमा}} (\emph{muqadmā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muqaddama}, \textquotedblleft{}what is put in front\textquotedblright{}, and so a case laid before a court. A case \textbf{\hi{चलता} \hi{है}}: it runs on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muqadmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muqadmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adālat meṁ cor kā muqadmā do sāl se cal rahā hai.} — The thief's case has been going on in court for two years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to search for, then the Hindi for to arrest, then say \emph{muqadmā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{मुक़दमा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A court case; a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{सज़ा} (sazā)}{सज़ा (sazā)}]{\hi{सज़ा} (sazā) — a punishment; a sentence}

\label{lesson:HI-C295-saza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to arrest, then the Hindi for a court case.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सज़ा}}
\textbf{\hi{सज़ा}} — \emph{sazā} — \textquotedblleft{}a punishment; a sentence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{आपको} \hi{सज़ा} \hi{का} \hi{डर} \hi{है}, \hi{तो} \hi{सच} \hi{कहिए।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āpko sazā kā ḍar hai, to sac kahiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you are afraid of punishment, tell the truth.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{सज़ा}} (\emph{sazā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{sazā}, \textquotedblleft{}what is fitting, what one deserves\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\hi{अदालत} \hi{ने} \hi{चोर} \hi{को} \hi{दो} \hi{साल} \hi{की} \hi{सज़ा} \hi{दी}}, the court gave the thief two years.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sazā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sazā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āpko sazā kā ḍar hai, to sac kahiye.} — If you are afraid of punishment, tell the truth.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to arrest, then the Hindi for a court case, then say \emph{sazā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सज़ा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A punishment; a sentence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{जुर्माना} (jurmānā)}{जुर्माना (jurmānā)}]{\hi{जुर्माना} (jurmānā) — a fine}

\label{lesson:HI-C295-jurmana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a court case, then the Hindi for a punishment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{जुर्माना}}
\textbf{\hi{जुर्माना}} — \emph{jurmānā} — \textquotedblleft{}a fine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{चोर} \hi{को} \hi{पाँच} \hi{हज़ार} \hi{रुपये} \hi{का} \hi{जुर्माना} \hi{भरना} \hi{पड़ा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cor ko pā̃c hazār rupaye kā jurmānā bharnā paṛā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief had to pay a fine of five thousand rupees.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{जुर्माना}} (\emph{jurmānā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{jurmāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a fine\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{jurm}, a crime: the money a crime costs. You \textbf{\hi{भरना}} a fine, fill it up, as you pay a bill.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jurmānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jurmānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cor ko pā̃c hazār rupaye kā jurmānā bharnā paṛā.} — The thief had to pay a fine of five thousand rupees.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a court case, then the Hindi for a punishment, then say \emph{jurmānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{जुर्माना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fine\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हथकड़ी} (hathkaṛī)}{हथकड़ी (hathkaṛī)}]{\hi{हथकड़ी} (hathkaṛī) — handcuffs}

\label{lesson:HI-C295-hathkari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a punishment, then the Hindi for a fine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हथकड़ी}}
\textbf{\hi{हथकड़ी}} — \emph{hathkaṛī} — \textquotedblleft{}handcuffs\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{पुलिस} \hi{चोर} \hi{को} \hi{हथकड़ी} \hi{में} \hi{अदालत} \hi{ले} \hi{गई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulis cor ko hathkaṛī meṁ adālat le gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police took the thief to court in handcuffs.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हथकड़ी}} (\emph{hathkaṛī}) joins \textbf{\hi{हाथ}}, hand, with \emph{kaṛī}, a metal ring, which CDIAL 2629 lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{kaṭa}: rings for the hands. The first part shortens, as \textbf{\hi{हाथ}} does in compounds.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hathkaṛī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hathkaṛī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pulis cor ko hathkaṛī meṁ adālat le gaī.} — The police took the thief to court in handcuffs.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a punishment, then the Hindi for a fine, then say \emph{hathkaṛī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from A Theft in the Lane to The Case in Court}

\label{lesson:HI-R295-review-288-295}



\begin{quote}
Say the Hindi for a theft and to steal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a theft, to steal, a watchman, a witness, outside
  \item a pickpocket, to snatch, to lunge, on the run, a chase
  \item a complaint, a report (to the police), to have written down, a police inspector, a lock-up
  \item an eyewitness, a statement, to recognize, suspicion, to stare
  \item a bandit, to rob, a robbery (by a gang), a gun, to tie up
  \item to cheat, a deception, a bribe, a crook, fake
  \item an investigation, a clue, a detective, evidence, to search for
  \item to arrest, a court case, a punishment, a fine, handcuffs
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A theft? (\textbf{\hi{चोरी}}, \emph{corī}.) To steal? (\textbf{\hi{चुराना}}, \emph{curānā}.) A watchman? (\textbf{\hi{चौकीदार}}, \emph{caukīdār}.) A witness? (\textbf{\hi{गवाह}}, \emph{gavāh}.) Outside? (\textbf{\hi{बाहर}}, \emph{bāhar}.) A pickpocket? (\textbf{\hi{जेबकतरा}}, \emph{jebkatrā}.) To snatch? (\textbf{\hi{छीनना}}, \emph{chīnnā}.) To lunge? (\textbf{\hi{झपटना}}, \emph{jhapaṭnā}.) On the run? (\textbf{\hi{फ़रार}}, \emph{farār}.) A chase? (\textbf{\hi{पीछा}}, \emph{pīchā}.) A complaint? (\textbf{\hi{शिकायत}}, \emph{śikāyat}.) A report (to the police)? (\textbf{\hi{रिपोर्ट}}, \emph{riporṭ}.) To have written down? (\textbf{\hi{लिखवाना}}, \emph{likhvānā}.) A police inspector? (\textbf{\hi{दरोगा}}, \emph{darogā}.) A lock-up? (\textbf{\hi{हवालात}}, \emph{havālāt}.) An eyewitness? (\textbf{\hi{चश्मदीद}}, \emph{caśmdīd}.) A statement? (\textbf{\hi{बयान}}, \emph{bayān}.) To recognize? (\textbf{\hi{पहचानना}}, \emph{pahcānnā}.) Suspicion? (\textbf{\hi{शक}}, \emph{śak}.) To stare? (\textbf{\hi{घूरना}}, \emph{ghūrnā}.) A bandit? (\textbf{\hi{डाकू}}, \emph{ḍākū}.) To rob? (\textbf{\hi{लूटना}}, \emph{lūṭnā}.) A robbery (by a gang)? (\textbf{\hi{डकैती}}, \emph{ḍakaitī}.) A gun? (\textbf{\hi{बंदूक़}}, \emph{bandūq}.) To tie up? (\textbf{\hi{बाँधना}}, \emph{bā̃dhnā}.) To cheat? (\textbf{\hi{ठगना}}, \emph{ṭhagnā}.) A deception? (\textbf{\hi{धोखा}}, \emph{dhokhā}.) A bribe? (\textbf{\hi{रिश्वत}}, \emph{riśvat}.) A crook? (\textbf{\hi{बदमाश}}, \emph{badmāś}.) Fake? (\textbf{\hi{नक़ली}}, \emph{naqlī}.) An investigation? (\textbf{\hi{तफ़्तीश}}, \emph{taftīś}.) A clue? (\textbf{\hi{सुराग़}}, \emph{surāġ}.) A detective? (\textbf{\hi{जासूस}}, \emph{jāsūs}.) Evidence? (\textbf{\hi{सबूत}}, \emph{sabūt}.) To search for? (\textbf{\hi{खोजना}}, \emph{khojnā}.) To arrest? (\textbf{\hi{गिरफ़्तार} \hi{करना}}, \emph{giraftār karnā}.) A court case? (\textbf{\hi{मुक़दमा}}, \emph{muqadmā}.) A punishment? (\textbf{\hi{सज़ा}}, \emph{sazā}.) A fine? (\textbf{\hi{जुर्माना}}, \emph{jurmānā}.) Handcuffs? (\textbf{\hi{हथकड़ी}}, \emph{hathkaṛī}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
